entry.title: Where in the wiring is the turn? (our own pre-registered test, brain only, 6 Oct 2026): We turned the scrambled maps up until they were as busy as the real one. They still did not produce the turn: the wiring, not the amount of activity, makes it. Also: Scrambling only the inside of the map kept about -9% of the turn command and 69% of the escape signal. (-9% means none: the far-side command was absent in all 6 trials) and With the escape neuron silenced, the turn command stayed. (expected: no giant fibre to DNa02 connections). Shown with every caveat in the chart: brain only, 7 drives await body runs, n per arm, a faster input checked first. New chart, census diagram and share card.

'Is it AI?' as a catalogue field: trained_class on all 116 records (45 of 83 graded projects have a trained, learning or search-tuned part in the main path); a filter on Projects, a chart, an updated answer and the field documented on For AI agents.

FlyWire's CC BY vs CC BY-NC conflict stays open; MANC and larva L1 sizes not stated. New answer 'What do I have to download?'.

Does it actually run? Our headless-browser check of six fly-brain demos (Chromium 154, Linux, no GPU, 3 Oct 2026; not a play test): Fly Worker, FLY67 and flybrain.app ran (17.55, 33.28 and 12.72 MB); FlyLeno and Help the Fly Escape loaded, then froze in our no-GPU browser; fly-brain (Lulzx) stopped at our 1.6 GB memory limit. No demo computed on a server. New chart 'What your browser downloads to run a fly brain' and a results table.
